title: Myth: you only owe sales tax in your home state
label: Myth vs fact

hook.text: "I only charge sales tax in *my* state."

lines: Maya runs a Shopify store from Texas.

She has never filed in New Jersey.

captions.instagram:
Myth: you only charge sales tax in your home state.
Fact: once your sales into another state pass that state's line, you may have to register, collect and file there too.

✔️ New Jersey example: more than $100,000 of sales into NJ, or 200 or more separate NJ sales, in the current or prior calendar year.
✔️ Sales through a marketplace like Etsy or Amazon: the marketplace generally collects for you.
✔️ Sales on your own Shopify site: that part is on you.
✔️ Every state sets its own line, so check each state you ship to.

Big holiday season? Look at your sales by state before January.
Send this to a friend who sells on Shopify.

Source: NJ Division of Taxation, Remote Sellers. General information, not advice for your situation.

captions.youtube_description: Myth: you only collect sales tax in your home state. Fact: many states require out-of-state sellers to register and collect once sales into the state pass a threshold. New Jersey example: more than $100,000 of NJ sales or 200 or more separate NJ transactions in the current or prior calendar year. Marketplace facilitators like Etsy and Amazon generally collect on marketplace sales; sales on your own site are your responsibility. Every state sets its own threshold. Source: NJ Division of Taxation, Remote Sellers.
